A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LICORICE and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-C. The original methods and experiments can be matched despite the changed title, reorganized presentation, and expanded evaluation.

before.justification: V1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments on PixelCartPole, DoorKey, and DynamicObstacles, including budget sweeps, GPT-4o annotation results, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds Boxing and Pong experiments, simulated concept interventions, data-diversity measurements, and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: V2 adds a substantive final training stage for Boxing and Pong: reinitialize the action network, freeze the learned concept encoder, and optimize PPO plus a KL penalty anchoring the new policy to the previous policy (Section 3; Appendix A.4). V1 ends with ordinary interleaved training. The original bottleneck, decorrelation, and disagreement-selection components remain.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual training and evaluation on Atari Boxing and Pong, extending coverage to two-frame player-position concepts and multi-frame ball/paddle dynamics. The three original environments remain under shortened names. These additions substantially expand the environments and concept spaces evaluated.

E2.justification: The fixed-budget comparator set remains Sequential-Q, Disagreement-Q, Random-Q, and CPM. V2 additionally includes the three budget-constrained baselines in the varying-budget comparison, previously reported for LICORICE and its GPT-4o variant (Figure 3; Table 8). Appendix B.6 also adds a vote-entropy acquisition comparator.

E3.justification: V2 introduces concept-noise/intervention protocols, Atari-specific training budgets, five-pixel tolerance for Boxing concept accuracy, and shifted reward normalization for Pong. Appendix A.4 also revises existing reported settings: the value-function coefficient changes from 1 to 0.5, and acceptance probability changes from 0.05 to 0.02 for PixelCartPole and 0.1 for the Minigrid environments. These reporting changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations and agent-behavior example, v2 adds noisy-concept intervention curves and counterfactual examples, Boxing ablations, a nearest-neighbor data-diversity analysis, a hyperparameter sensitivity study, and a disagreement-versus-entropy comparison (Figures 4-5; Appendix B.4-B.6). These investigate several previously untested mechanisms and robustness questions.

E5.justification: Both versions specify the same five training seeds, report standard deviations, and show ablation learning curves with 95% confidence intervals calculated using 1000 bootstrap samples. The expanded results do not introduce a different repeated-run or statistical-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The original three-environment scores are retained in corresponding tables. V2 adds substantial new results: Table 5 reports normalized reward/concept error of 1.00/0.05 for Boxing and 1.00/0.24 for Pong, plus new budget, intervention, and sensitivity findings. Some new entries conflict with retained summaries: PixelCartPole Disagreement-Q reward at budget 500 is 0.39 in Table 8 but 0.36 in Table 5, without an explained setting difference.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the value-function conditioning from s0 = s to st = s and introduces mathematical definitions for the nearest-neighbor diversity statistic and vote-entropy acquisition score (Appendix B.4/B.6). The original disagreement formulas remain unchanged, and neither version contains a theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains label-efficient concept-based RL using the same three principal components. V2 extends the abstract's quantified claim from at most 500 labels in three environments to include at most 5000 labels in two more complex environments, and explicitly frames automated annotation costs as part of the problem.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving early optimization traps, large Atari concept spaces, and inherently dissimilar neighboring states reducing the importance of decorrelation in DynamicObstacles. Appendix C.1 adds scaling limitations involving irrelevant concepts and prerequisite concept learning. Most earlier VLM, concept-design, and broader-impact discussions are retained or relocated.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-release statement and repository link, Atari concept definitions and prompts, domain-specific training settings, the KL penalty weight, and additional resource estimates. It also clarifies Random-Q's acceptance rate. However, v1's explicit observation-resolution disclosure is omitted. The existing CNN/MLP architecture description is largely relocated and expanded rather than replaced.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for Atari, OCAtari, VIPER, PPO, label-free concept models, compositional generalization, and proposed future directions. Related work briefly distinguishes Shao et al. (2024) by its focus on human task demonstrations; the earlier Radford et al. reference is removed. The principal research positioning and related-work categories remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Preliminaries are reorganized around concept policy models, experimental setup is consolidated, research questions are reordered and expanded, and architecture details and limitations move into the appendices. This substantially changes the explanatory structure beyond simply inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: V2 adds a method overview, benchmark and budget plots, intervention illustrations, and a sensitivity chart. Several main-text tables become plots with detailed appendix tables; the DoorKey configuration figure gains concept annotations. The separate final-ablation bar chart is removed while corresponding tables and learning curves remain. The document also adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the paper beyond its original three-environment demonstration: Atari evaluations broaden empirical support, baseline budget curves better test label efficiency, and simulated interventions and supplementary analyses directly examine interpretability and robustness. The clearer method presentation and expanded reproduction information also help. These gains outweigh the omitted resolution details and unexplained cross-table discrepancies, although those inconsistencies limit confidence in some individual results.
